payload.name: superior-pharyngeal-constrictor
payload.scope: People made the superior-pharyngeal-constrictor construct to map the uppermost pharyngeal constrictor muscle band that forms the posterior and lateral walls of the superior pharynx, enabling clinicians to localize pharyngeal constriction defects and retropharyngeal abscesses.

definition.body: The superior pharyngeal constrictor is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the quadrate sheet of muscle forming the uppermost band of the posterior and lateral walls of the pharynx. Parameters: (1) the origins - pterygoid hamulus, pterygomandibular raphe (shared with the buccinator), and the medial pterygoid plate of the sphenoid bone; (2) the insertion - the pharyngeal tubercle of the occipital bone and the pharyngeal raphe, a midline tendon where the fibers of both sides interdigitate; (3) the fiber orientation - lower fibers run inferiorly, upper fibers overlap the middle constrictor; (4) the aperture - the stylopharyngeus nerve passes through between the superior and middle bands; (5) the clinical significance - landmark for pharyngeal surgery, origin of superior constrictor palsy in stroke, and site of pharyngoplasty for velopharyngeal insufficiency. It persists as a standard anatomical structure in human anatomy texts, otolaryngology references, and swallowing assessment protocols. e.g.: the superior pharyngeal constrictor in Gray's Anatomy, 42nd edition by Drake; the pharyngeal raphe during constrictor repair in Cummings Otolaryngology, 6th edition; stylopharyngeus nerve passing through the constrictor in Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th edition | not: the middle-pharyngeal-constrictor (the intermediate band arising from the hyoid bone, a distinct muscle layer); the inferior-pharyngeal-constrictor arising from the cricoid and thyroid cartilages, a distinct muscle layer; the buccinator (the facial muscle sharing the pterygomandibular raphe, not a pharyngeal muscle) [formal: constrictor pharyngis superior | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

payload.scope: People made the middle-pharyngeal-constrictor construct to map the intermediate pharyngeal constrictor muscle band arising from the hyoid apparatus, enabling clinicians to assess swallowing mechanics and pharyngeal wall abnormalities.

definition.body: The middle pharyngeal constrictor is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the fan-shaped sheet of muscle forming the intermediate band of the posterior and lateral walls of the pharynx. Parameters: (1) the origins - the lesser and greater horns of the hyoid bone and the hyoidothyroid ligament; (2) the insertion - the pharyngeal raphe and overlapping fibers posteriorly where it fuses with the superior constrictor above and the inferior constrictor below; (3) the fiber arrangement - fibers fan superiorly to overlap the superior constrictor and inferiorly to be overlapped by the inferior constrictor; (4) the aperture - the stylopharyngeus muscle passes between the superior and middle constrictors, and the glossopharyngeal nerve and tonsillar artery pass between the middle and inferior constrictors; (5) the clinical significance - landmark in tonsillectomy (the constrictor is the bed from which the tonsil is dissected), site of pharyngeal diverticula, and reference for pharyngeal pacing. It persists as a standard anatomical structure in human anatomy texts, otolaryngology references, and swallowing assessment protocols. e.g.: the middle pharyngeal constrictor in Gray's Anatomy, 42nd edition by Drake; the tonsil bed defined by the middle constrictor in Cummings Otolaryngology, 6th edition; stylopharyngeus passing between the constrictors in Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th edition | not: superior-pharyngeal-constrictor (uppermost band from pterygoid, distinct layer); inferior-pharyngeal-constrictor (lowest band from cricoid/thyroid, distinct layer); stylopharyngeus (passes between constrictors, not a constrictor) [formal: constrictor pharyngis medius | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

definition.body: The inferior pharyngeal constrictor is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the lowest and broadest band of muscle forming the posterior and lateral walls of the inferior pharynx. Parameters: (1) the origins - the oblique and transverse parts arising from the cricoid cartilage (thyrocricoid membrane and posterior lamina) and the thyroid cartilage (oblique line); (2) the insertion - the pharyngeal raphe posteriorly where fibers from both sides interdigitate; (3) the fiber arrangement - lower fibers run horizontally to the raphe, upper fibers (cricopharyngeus part) run obliquely upward and medially, forming the lower boundary of the inferior constrictor; (4) the apertures - the esophagus passes through inferiorly at the pharyngoesophageal junction, the internal laryngeal nerve pierces between the superior and inferior bands, and the superior laryngeal artery passes through the same gap; (5) the clinical significance - the cricopharyngeus part forms the upper esophageal sphincter (Cricopharyngeal dysfunction causes dysphagia and Zenker's diverticulum through Killian's dehiscence between the thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus parts. It persists as a standard anatomical structure in human anatomy texts, otolaryngology references, and swallowing assessment protocols. e.g.: the inferior pharyngeal constrictor in Gray's Anatomy, 42nd edition by Drake; the cricopharyngeal bar seen on barium swallow per Cummings Otolaryngology, 6th edition; Killian's dehiscence at the thyropharyngeus-cricopharyngeus junction in Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th edition | not: middle-pharyngeal-constrictor (intermediate band from hyoid, distinct layer); superior-pharyngeal-constrictor (uppermost band from pterygoid, distinct layer); cricopharyngeus-muscle (the transverse band forming the upper esophageal sphincter, a specialized part of this muscle) [formal: constrictor pharyngis inferior | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

payload.note: Law 8 dependency test: the hypopharynx definition explicitly lists the recurrent laryngeal nerve in parameter (4) neurovascular supply. The recurrent laryngeal nerve provides sensory innervation to the mucosa of the hypopharynx. Without this nerve, the hypopharynx would lose a constitutive component of its innervation — the construct as carved would cease to be what it is defined as. The nerve is enumerated as a specific parameter of the hypopharynx map, not merely adjacent to it. Type DEPENDS_ON, direction dependent-to-needed. Sense uses each endpoint as its definition carves it.
